prompt:
You are P1 in a three-player live auction. Highest final coins plus owned printed values wins; ties shared. Eight simultaneous action rounds maximum. Lots have printed values 4, 6, 10, sold in order. One action each round: [bid: N] commits a sealed nonnegative integer bid on the current lot; a bid cannot exceed your coins. Commitments cannot be changed. The lot resolves when all three have committed. Highest bid wins; ties favor the earliest commitment round, then lowest seat number. The winner pays the bid, gains the lot, then receives a three-coin auction commission. [wait: 1] waits; sealed rival bids should remain private. [buy: 1] buys a catalog item for one coin, printed value one; catalog items are not auction wins. Buying is unavailable while your bid is pending. [close: 1] settles after all three lots are sold. [clerk: standings] asks for scores. While committed you can wait, ask the clerk, or request settlement. All unresolved lots remain unsold at the eight-round horizon. Only resolved bids are normally public. Other players choose their own actions.
{"round": 1, "scores": [12, 12, 12], "coins": [12, 12, 12], "owned": [[], [], []], "lot": 0, "lots": [4, 6, 10], "committed": [false, false, false], "own_bid": null, "feedback": "Game begins.", "last_resolution": []}
reply: **Reason:** The decisive mechanic here is that a lot only resolves when *all three* players commit, and unresolved lots stay unsold at the horizon. So whoever wins lot 1 (value 4) at a bid of 6 or less ends at 13 vs. rivals' 12 — then can simply never commit on the remaining lots, freezing the game at that standing. Bids are only paid by winners, so a losing sealed bid costs nothing. Bidding 6 maximizes my chance to win lot 1 while still staying strictly ahead (7 would only tie me at 12; 8+ would put me behind). Committing immediately in round 1 also secures the tie-break (earliest round, lowest seat) in case rivals match 6. Plan: if I win, stall forever; if I lose, keep my 12 coins and fight on lot 2. [bid: 6]
